proposals.before: There was also the Iron-Forbidden State: in Shengzong's Chongxi year 17 it begged troops to assist the attack on Western Xia; the edict refused.
proposals.after: There was also the Iron-Forbidden State: in Xingzong's Chongxi year 17 it begged troops to assist the attack on Western Xia; the edict refused.
proposals.reason: Chinese 興宗重熙十七年 names Xingzong, not Shengzong; Chongxi was Xingzong's reign.

proposals.before: The Iron-Forbidden State once asked in Chongxi year 17 to join an attack on Western Xia; the court denied the request.
proposals.after: In Xingzong's Chongxi year 17 the Iron-Forbidden State once asked to join an attack on Western Xia; the court denied the request.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 興宗 (Xingzong), who is named in the Chinese as the reigning emperor for Chongxi 17.

proposals.before: Small Goryeo still drained Liao forces again and again—perhaps its rugged ground alone could explain it.
proposals.after: Goryeo was a small state yet repeatedly cost Liao armies—was it not because its difficult terrain was enough to rely on?
proposals.reason: Chinese 險阻足恃 means the rugged terrain was sufficient to rely on, not that it was hard to rely on; the rhetorical question affirms terrain as an asset.

proposals.before: Goryeo was a small state yet repeatedly cost Liao armies—was it not because its terrain was hard to rely on?
proposals.after: Goryeo was a small state yet repeatedly cost Liao armies—was it not because its difficult terrain was sufficient to rely on?
proposals.reason: Literal reverses 足恃: the terrain is relied upon as a defense, not unreliable.

proposals.before: Only when Song's Taizong attacked Northern Han could Liao not relieve the target; otherwise Liao mostly lost, and wins rarely paid for themselves.
proposals.after: Only when Song's Taizong campaigned against Northern Han could Liao not save it; otherwise Liao mostly lost, and even victories did not repay the cost.
proposals.reason: “Relieve the target” obscures 遼不能救: Liao could not rescue Northern Han; align with the Chinese referent.

decisions.reason: Chinese 興宗重熙十七年 names Xingzong; Shengzong (聖宗) is a different Liao emperor, and Chongxi was Xingzong's era.
The Chinese explicitly names 興宗 before 重熙十七年; the idiomatic omits that temple name, and restoring Xingzong matches the source.
The idiomatic already treats rugged ground as the explanation for Goryeo's success; it does not reverse 足恃. The proposed rewrite mainly restyles the rhetorical question.
足恃 means the terrain was sufficient to rely on as a defense; 'hard to rely on' reverses that sense.

decisions.after: Only when Song's Taizong campaigned against Northern Han could Liao not save it; otherwise Song mostly lost, and even victories did not repay the cost.
decisions.reason: 遼不能救 correctly means Liao could not rescue Northern Han, but 餘多敗衄 continues the Song subject (clarified by s0221 on China's loss of the five passes); the proposal still wrongly makes Liao the loser.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 宋惟太宗征北漢，遼不能救，餘多敗衄
